_doc: LOCKED template bank. Agents choose `template`, optional `variant`, and fill ONLY the listed slots. Slot kinds: cutout = transparent PNG subject (auto background removal), photo = rectangular photo or clip, photos/objects = arrays, device = bank device with screen rect, string = short text. `variants` lists the layouts a variant number selects (variant % count). `maxWords` / `maxLineChars` are hard limits for the text block.

type-center.use: Pure kinetic typography. Hooks, punchlines, abstract statements, anything with no concrete visual. The workhorse between visual scenes.

bigWord.note: optional faint giant word behind the text

object-hero.use: One concrete object/subject the line is about (a heart, a watch, a lantern, an eye). Text above the object.

object-side.use: Object on one side, 2–4 short stacked lines on the other. Good for a list-like or rhythmic sentence ("It's not / just / what").

word-behind.use: Depth reveal: a giant word or letter behind a subject standing in front of it. Use for the single most important word of a beat. The bigWord is removed from the small caption line.

photo-full.use: Establishing shots and places (a room, a street at night, a face). Full-bleed graded photo or clip with a slow Ken Burns move.

photo-framed.use: A photo presented as evidence/memory: glowing rimmed card (noir) or pinned polaroid (atelier).

card-stack.use: Accumulation: several moments/people/examples. 2–4 photo cards fly in one after another on the narration.

tv-screen.use: Watching / being watched / memory / broadcast. A vintage TV with a photo on its screen (an eye, a face, a place).

phone-screen.use: Modern life / scrolling / messages / a call. A phone rises; its screen shows a photo or 1–3 words.

pinned-note.use: A clue, a note, a detail on paper. Torn note pinned to the board; words printed on it; optional object on the note.

split-panel.use: A person or place revealed on a tall panel swinging open like a door; text beside it. Good for introducing a character.

scatter.use: A cluster of related objects around one phrase (clues, belongings, symbols). 2–5 small cutouts pop in on the narration.

figure-spotlight.use: A character on stage: person cutout in a spotlight, text beside. Introductions, confessions, a lone figure.

outro-hold.use: The final line only. Calm hold, optional small object, fades to the ground colour.

transitions.blur-zoom: outgoing zooms and blurs out, incoming settles from zoom (noir default)
transitions.whip-left: fast horizontal whip with directional blur
transitions.whip-right: fast horizontal whip with directional blur
transitions.whip-up: fast vertical whip with directional blur
transitions.flash: warm light-leak flash on the cut (turns, revelations)
transitions.zoom-through: camera flies through the outgoing scene
transitions.slide-up: incoming scene slides up over the old one like paper
